hints: State both the total quantity that is unchanged and the external-force condition.
walkthrough: The principle concerns the total momentum of the system, rather than the momentum of an individual object.
For an isolated system with no resultant external force, total momentum remains constant.
Equivalently, total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after it.

ai_rubric.observable: States that total momentum remains constant, or that total momentum before an interaction equals total momentum after it.
Includes the isolated-system or no-resultant-external-force condition.

hints: Resolve momentum separately parallel and perpendicular to the initial direction; the initial perpendicular momentum is zero.
Use the perpendicular equation to relate v and w, then substitute into the parallel equation.
walkthrough: Take the initial motion as the x-direction. Initial momentum is 2m × 5.0 = 10m in x and zero in y.
Conservation in x gives 10m = 2mv cos 30° + 3mw cos 30°.
Conservation in y gives 2mv sin 30° = 3mw sin 30°, so v = 3w / 2.
Substitute v = 1.5w into the x equation: 10 = cos 30°(2 × 1.5w + 3w) = 6w cos 30°.
Thus w = 1.9 m s⁻¹ and v = 2.9 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Writes a momentum-conservation equation parallel to the initial motion.
Writes the perpendicular momentum equation and obtains v = 3w / 2, or an equivalent relation.

hints: The stopping force removes the object's kinetic energy over the stated stopping distance.
Calculate the initial kinetic energy, then use work done = force × distance.
walkthrough: When the object stops, its initial kinetic energy is transferred by the constant stopping force.
The force acts opposite to the displacement, so its magnitude satisfies work done = Fs.
F = 75.6 / 0.050 = 1512 N, giving a stopping-force magnitude of 1.5 × 10³ N.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the initial kinetic energy as 76 J.
Relates the stopping-force magnitude to work done divided by stopping distance.
Obtains a stopping-force magnitude of 1500 N, or 1.5 × 10³ N.
